Twelve-point follow-up: local PLS exits and financing conditions
29 September 2026. Follow-up to the skeptical review and the clarification that redemption means a
local pDAI exit into PLS, WPLS or the exact inherited native-wrapping WETH contract. No Ethereum
bridge-out or external-dollar payout is required. The dollar reference remains a measurement convention
for local execution. Governance and operator control are scenario assumptions where not independently
established.
The maintained white paper (main paper) incorporates the completed findings. The financing,
mathematical and local-evidence studies below contain detailed derivations and records. This follow-up
strengthens the conditional argument without claiming that every deployed financing path is proved
executable.
Findings for each examined point
Point Work completed and conclusion Remaining boundary
1. Meanings of backing Defined source custody, source
solvency, withdrawal timing, funded
acceptance and the holder's local PLS
exit separately. A mechanically
accepted weak claim can finance a
finite purchase.
Solvency is still necessary for a claim
of solvent ongoing financing; it is not
a universal precondition for a local
swap.
2. Funding source Added full outright-sale, borrowing,
issuer and relayer ledgers identifying
who pays existing local assets, who
receives each claim, and when
liabilities are due.
Exact executable bids/loan terms for
the proposed deployed source receipts
remain stipulated.
3. Exact identities Identified a historical copied-DAI/WPLS
pool and native conversion for
canonical WPLS and inherited WETH.
Existing Aave receipt/wrapper
identities remain defined by their own
contracts.
Economic native-unit equivalence
does not make different token
addresses interchangeable inside
pools or collateral adapters.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 454

Point Work completed and conclusion Remaining boundary
4. Governance versus current state Retained explicit classification of
adjustable settings, changed
integrations and new
implementations. Effective authorized
governance can conceivably remove
some current blockers.
A new detailed permission-path
extension did not reach completed
review; no new exact-role readiness
claim is promoted from it.
5. Aave cap barriers Retained verified earlier distinctions
between zero Portal capacity and
independent DAI/USDT supply-cap
constraints. Each subsequent wrapper
operation must also pass its own limits
at its execution state.
The additional detailed deposit-limit/
permission review remains
incomplete; raising a single cap is not
treated as proof of an executable full
route.
6. Portal and ordinary debt Closed a 100-unit Portal example with
99.9 market proceeds plus 0.1
contributed underlying; ordinary
repayment remains separate.
Distinguished underlying-funded and
aT oken-funded debt repayment,
including a conditional discounted-
claim benefit to an eligible borrower.
Full settlement consumes its assigned
cash. Third-party payment does not
transfer another borrower's collateral,
and no historical arbitrage profit is
asserted.
7. Pending transfers and return Retained settled-state versus in-flight
custody accounting and distinguished
optional source return from the pDAI
holder's local exit.
Exact cancellation/finality/return rights
remain implementation-specific when
source backing is claimed. None is
silently imposed as an Ethereum exit
requirement.
8. Intermediate funding Added per-actor, per-asset cash
constraints at every step, not merely
at the end. Loan maturities and
operating costs belong at their actual
due times.
No instantaneous cross-chain
financing or future receivable is
counted as current local cash without
a funded advance.
9. Shared resources Consolidated source claims, collateral
pledges, relayer inventory, pool cash
and native-wrapper backing. Funds
may be reused after actual return, but
not independently counted twice.
A combined deployed-route budget
still needs state-dependent execution
curves and exclusive capital
allocations.
10. Assets returning to market Modeled holder exits separately from
Aave withdrawals, released collateral,
issuer redemption and source returns.
Added an inventory-constrained sell-
above-target example that replenishes
PLS under assumed appreciation.
Deposits/repayments are not
permanent burns. Selling retained
pDAI uses inventory and may affect
markets; resulting PLS is not costless
profit.
11. Bounded support Evaluated six thirty-event fee-
inclusive scenarios, two appreciation
scenarios, and two alternative sell-
side checkpoints. Independently
checked the six original scenarios and
sell-side roots.
Results require the stated funded
inventory, timing and reference path.
They do not calibrate real selling
pressure or prove continuous support
under arbitrary flows.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 455

Point Work completed and conclusion Remaining boundary
12. Evidence and reproduction Verified one historical pDAI-to-WPLS
branch followed by aggregate native
payout, pinned local-pool reserves,
and exact native-wrapper behavior.
Prepared selected evidence and
explicit mathematical batches with
hashes.
Historical observations are not live
quotes or source-financing
provenance. Selected publication
evidence is not the complete audit
archive or independent node
authentication.
What is now positively established within scope
The holder-side exit is no longer only an abstract example: a historical local swap and native withdrawal
sequence has been reconciled. Its source financing is not attributed to the thesis. The exact inherited
WETH and canonical WPLS wrappers provide native PLS conversion mechanics, so the theory need not
prove an Ethereum redemption process to use these as local exit forms.
The financial argument now includes more than an outright sale. Borrowing, eligible issuance, Portal
settlement and relayer inventory exchange have complete illustrative ledgers. None requires free
creation of local purchasing assets. Each identifies the provider of the inventory and resulting exposure.
This is a positive conditional composition result, rather than a list of unconnected protocol names.
The dynamic argument now includes a funded sequence of local exits with trading fees and a separate
sale of retained pDAI when an assumed PLS appreciation moves the local dollar-reference quote above
target. It shows how a two-sided policy could use existing inventories, while exposing budget and
reference-price failure cases. It does not prove that establishing a peg causes PLS appreciation.
Numerical results and limits
At the illustrative 0.3% fee and starting reserves, the initial purchase costs 2,175,295,195.262100 PLS.
With 400 million additional support PLS, thirty successive 1,000-pDAI exits each receive 10 million PLS at
the fixed $0.0001 reference. The 29 intermediate purchases cost 290,871,239.738011 PLS. These are
local PLS payments; there is no bridge-out cash flow.
If the reference instead rises at event 16, fewer PLS are needed per dollar of pDAI. Under an explicitly
separate sell-side policy, a 50% rise permits the modeled operator to exchange 70,153.484465 retained
pDAI for 572,788,016.391764 PLS while restoring the next 1,000-pDAI quote to the target. Doubling the
reference gives a different feasible branch: 130,138.650678 pDAI sold for 920,191,644.708543 PLS. The
branches are alternatives, not additive proceeds.
These positive results are financed scenarios. They do not remove exact-token compatibility, role and
cap checks, amount-specific liquidity, fees, timing, debt obligations or counterparty responses. A local
PLS target changes the required exit asset; it does not eliminate the funding question.
Methods, validation and unfinished scope
The mathematical models are offline Decimal calculations. No transaction, governance vote, deployment
or state-changing simulation was performed. The economic review independently recomputed all 180
events in the initial six scenarios using bisection rather than the quadratic solver; conservation and
results agreed. It separately checked both sell-side roots and inventory bounds. The two buy-only
appreciation branches use the same validated solver and run its per-event conservation and cash
checks.
pDAI stabilization thesis · 4 October 2026 456

An automated review restriction left the contract-permission extension incomplete. That subreview was
not treated as completed verification. Its unfinished detailed role and wrapper-limit work is not used to
claim deployed readiness. Completed earlier protocol findings remain cited; the independent financing
and local-exit work continued within its own scope.
The research suite passed 63 tests and 82 subtests after both mathematical scripts were added. The
sell-side checkpoint additionally has independent formula/numerical checks and asserts token
conservation and inventory limits. Document and artifact checks are recorded with the final selected
publication bundle; the old experiments retain their original identities.
Supporting studies
Financing families, debt, settlement and local exit accounting (Appendix 42).
Fee-inclusive support, appreciation and sell-side equations (Appendix 43).
Historical local exit and exact native-wrapper evidence (Appendix 41).
Earlier Portal accounting and sampled reserve constraints (Appendix 17).
Original two-round skeptical review (Appendix 59).
